{{Quote|Reports indicate that thousands were killed in the coup, and that the former ruling family is now in exile.|Holonet News|<ref name="HNN 46" />}}
The '''royal family''' of Pergitor ruled over the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pergitor]] as a despotic [[Monarchy/Legends|monarchy]]<ref name="GG6" /> for at least seventy [[Standard year/Legends|years]] until the [[Church of Infinite Perception/Legends|Church of Infinite Perception]] [[Coup on Pergitor|claimed]] Pergitor<ref name="HNN 46 /> in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]].<ref name="Date" /> Their reign banned open dissent and was characterized by very strict conservative rules, inspired by the philosophy of [[Jesa Corporation]]'s [[Jesa Corporation's founder|founder]], who the family descended from.<ref name="HNN 46 /> 

Around [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|46|regional/1337_4.html|Pergitor Coup Leaves Thousands Dead}}, set on the date 13:3:7 and corresponding to the last [[Standard day/Legends|day]] of [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] according to the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]], states that fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] have passed since the young liberal's coup, therefore dating the coup to around [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]].</ref> many young Pergitor citizens&mdash;including some younger members of the royal family&mdash;sparked a liberal movement on Pergitor by watching prohibited [[Holodrama/Legends|holodramas]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] illegal goods such as synthetic drugs, shifting public opinion in favor of a less strict way of living. This led to a reform of the law by the royal family which granted freedom to Pergitor's inhabitants for fifteen years.<ref name="GG6" /> After the Church's coup,<ref name="Date" /> its [[The Preceptor|leader]] [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] the family from Pergitor,<ref name="GG6" /> which was mentioned in [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 47|"Pergitor Coup Leaves Thousands Dead"]], a news story published in CoCo District Edition of the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].<ref name="HNN 46" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Gg6-1.jpg|thumb|right|200px|''Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters'' marked the first mention of the Royal family of Pergitor.]]
The royal family of Pergitor was first mentioned in [[West End Games]]' ''[[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters]]'' from [[1990]], authored by [[Mark Rein-Hagen]] and [[Stewart Wieck]].<ref name="GG6" /> Despite it not giving a precise date for the events it covers, the guides are supplements to West End Games' [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']] which is set in the years after the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] but before [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] from [[1980]].<ref name="SWRPG">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''</ref> Dating the supplement to the time period of the core rulebook would place the coup and subsequent exile of the family between [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] and [[12 BBY/Legends|12 BBY]],<ref name="Date2">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' is set in the years after {{Film|IV}} but before {{Film|V}}, which corresponds to the time period between [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As ''[[Galaxy Guide 6: Tramp Freighters]]'' states the coup happened fifteen [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior, that would place the event between [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]] and [[12 BBY/Legends|12 BBY]]. Additionally the liberal uprising is said to have happened twenty-five years before, placing the event between [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]] and [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] following the [[Proclamation of the New Order|reorganization]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]].<ref name="ROTS Novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> The liberal movements on Pergitor would fall on a different date too, between [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]] and [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]].<ref name="Date2" />

On [[March 7]], [[2002]]<ref name="HNN46 date">Per {{JCFCite|url=posts/6042498|board=Literature|thread=The Official HoloNetNews Discussion Thread|user=IAmTheDarkSide|date=2002-03-14|time=5:40 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220914072556/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-official-holonetnews-discussion-thread.5990764/page-4#post-6042498}}, [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 47|''HoloNet News Vol. 531'' #47]] was released on [[March 14]], [[2002]]. As [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News]] segments were published weekly, and {{Hnn|46||HoloNet News Vol. 531 #46}} was the previous published issue, it must have been released on [[March 7]] of the same year.</ref> "Pergitor Coup Leaves Thousands Dead," an article<ref name="HNN 46" /> written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and [[Paul Ens]],<ref name="HNN Credits">{{HoloNetNewsWeb||credits.html|Credits}}</ref> and published in [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 46|''HoloNet News Vol. 531'' #46]] on the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News website]].<ref name="HNN 46" /> The article documented the [[Church of Infinite Perception/Legends|Church's]] coup on Pergitor,<ref name="HNN 46" /> dating the event to 23 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]] and subsequently preponing all of Pergitor's history by about eight years.<ref name="Date" /><ref name="Date2" />
